blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The World Trade Organization (WTO) has more than doubled its global merchandise trade growth forecast for 2026, as surging demand for artificial intelligence (AI) equipment, particularly from Asian manufacturers, has outweighed disruptions caused by the war in the Middle East. In its latest Global Trade Outlook and Statistics report, the Geneva-based organization raised its merchandise trade volume growth projection to 3.9 percent from 1.9 percent in March. READ: WTO sees progress in PH trade reforms WTO said the upward revision largely reflects stronger-than-expected investments in AI infrastructure, which have driven demand for semiconductors, servers and other electronic components.
